title: Senior asks: read() gives ['id' => '1'] from a CSV. Your test expects ['id' => 1]. assertEquals acts like ==, assertSame like ===. What does this print?
explain: CSV values are always strings. assertEquals uses loose compare, so '1' equals 1 and the test passes. assertSame is strict and fails. Use assertSame so the test shows the real type your API returns.

title: Senior asks: your boss wants XML files too. FileService gets a list of FileActionsInterface objects. What is the smallest change?
options: Add XmlFileActions with getFormat() 'xml', read(), write(), and add it to the list in index.php
Add an if ($ext === 'xml') branch inside FileService::read()
Copy CsvFileActions and rename it, then change FileController
explain: FileService finds the right class by getFormat(). A new class that implements the interface, plus one new item in the list in index.php, is enough. FileService and FileController stay untouched. This is the point of the interface: add code, do not edit working code.

title: Senior asks: write() saves JSON with JSON_PRETTY_PRINT. What does this print (bytes: compact, pretty)? Is pretty a good choice here?
explain: Pretty print adds newlines and spaces: here 17 becomes 53 bytes. For files that people open and compare in git, it is a good trade. For a big file or an API answer it costs size and time. It is fine here: files are small and human-read.

pr.title: Sort the file list A-Z, ignore case
pr.author: copilot-helper
pr.body: b.csv sorted before A.json. Now the list is sorted without case.

explain: natcasesort() sorts, but it keeps the old keys. After sorting, the keys are like 1, 0, 2. json_encode() then makes an object {"1":"a.csv",...} and the jQuery list breaks. Call array_values() to renumber the keys.

title: PHP 8. Array keys are cast. What does this print?
explain: The string '1' becomes the integer key 1. true also becomes key 1, so 'b' overwrites 'a'. '01' is not a clean integer string, so it stays a string key. Result: 2 keys, and $a[1] is 'b'.

title: A class method is taken out of its object, like a jQuery callback. What does Node print?
explain: show() lost its object. Class code is strict, so this is undefined, and undefined.label throws a TypeError. Same problem as a callback with this. Fix: call obj.show(), use an arrow function, or bind(obj).

title: You fixed a typo and also started a new feature in the same file. You want a small PR with only the typo. What do you run?
options: git add -p, choose only the typo hunk, then commit
git add . and commit with a long message
git commit -a and fix it later
git stash and delete the stash
explain: git add -p shows each change (hunk) and lets you stage only the ones you want. The feature stays in your working folder for the next commit. Small, single-purpose commits are easier to review on Bitbucket.

title: composer.json has PSR-4 "App\\" => "src/". You add src/Service/Mailer.php (class App\Service\Mailer). Do you need composer dump-autoload?
options: No: PSR-4 finds the file from the class name when it is first used
Yes, always, or the class is not found
No, but only with composer update
explain: PSR-4 is a rule: namespace prefix + folder path = file path. The autoloader builds the path at run time, so a new file works at once if the name and the case match. You need dump-autoload for classmap rules or an optimized classmap (-o).
